item.title: Non-Pseudo-Arithmetic Hyperbolic 4-Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.05795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give three explicit finite-volume hyperbolic Coxeter lattices in dimension four whose adjoint trace fields are not totally real. They are the reflection groups of the Ma--Zheng polytopes $P_{11,6}$, $P_{11,7}$, $P_{11,8}$. The obstruction is contained in two cyclic products of the doubled unit-normal Gram matrix $A=2G$. Those products recover elements $s=\sqrt5$ and $u$ satisfying $$ (s-1)u^2+2(s-3)u+s-7=0. $$ After the embedding $s\mapsto-\sqrt5$, this quadratic has discriminant $8(1-\sqrt5)<0$. The cyclic-product field therefore has a complex place. Vinberg's identification of that field with the adjoint trace field and the Emery--Mila total-reality obstruction imply that the three lattices are not pseudo-arithmetic. Torsion-free orientation-preserving finite-index subgroups yield orientable noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic $4$-manifolds with the same obstruction. Exact computations check the census data and provide independent field and finite-volume certificates. A pinned Lean~4 development verifies the radical identity and the number-field obstruction. It also checks the lattice and manifold implications conditional on explicit geometric and literature hypotheses.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kolpakov

item.title: On the (in)finiteness of fixed characters in genus $3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a counterexample to the Putman--Wieland conjecture in genus $3$ and discuss some of its consequences.
item.dc:creator: Yixuan Fu

item.title: 3-manifold decision problems and Riemann hypotheses
item.description: arXiv:2611.06705v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Beginning with Kuperberg's work on unknot recognition, several fundamental decision problems in 3-manifold topology have been shown to be in coNP assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis. In this note, we explain how recent developments around the quasi-Riemann hypothesis yield unconditional versions of these results, leading for example to the first unconditional proof that 3-sphere recognition is in coNP.
item.dc:creator: John A. Baldwin, Steven Sivek

item.title: Chromatic Spherical and Renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants for Drinfeld Centers
item.description: arXiv:2611.06708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give invariants of pairs $(M,\Gamma)$ consisting of a closed connected oriented three-manifold and an oriented framed ribbon graph embedded in $M$ colored by a the Drinfeld center of a unimodular chromatic category $\mathcal C$. This invariant generalizes the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants of three-manifolds. We use Heegaard-Graph diagrams which represent the pair $(M,\Gamma)$ and use the data of a unimodular chromatic category and objects of the Drinfeld center to construct the invariant. We define a ribbon graph associated to embedded framed links to obtain an invariant of pairs $(M,L)$. We show that if $L$ is the empty link, then the invariant recovers the chromatic spherical invariant, and if $M$ is the three-sphere, then the invariant recovers the renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant from the Drinfeld center. The relationship is proven by recovering a chromatic structure for the center induced by that from $\mathcal C$. The main theorem of the paper demonstrates that if the graph is a link $L$ colored by a generator in the Drinfeld center, then we recover the chromatic spherical invariant of the surgery manifold $M(L)$, contributing to a proof of the relationship between the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants for unimodular chromatic categories, generalizing a recent result for unimodular Hopf algebras by Reina. To this end, we give a Heegaard diagram for $M(L)$ coming from the Heegaard-Link diagram representing the pair $(M,L)$.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Bridges, Shawn Cui, Nathan Geer

item.title: Odd and even fake quadrics isogenous to a product
item.description: arXiv:2611.06077v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A $\mathbb{Q}$-homology quadric is a smooth compact complex surface which has the same $\mathbb{Q}$-homology as a quadric surface, that is, the product of two $2$-dimensional spheres. It is called fake if it is minimal and not rational. Among them are the fake quadrics which are isogenous to a product of complex curves. In this paper, we determine the parity of the intersection forms of all fake quadrics isogenous to a product of unmixed type. In particular, we show that there are fake quadrics with odd intersection forms.
item.dc:creator: Fabrizio Catanese, JongHae Keum, Do Geun Kim, Kyoung-Seog Lee

item.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.06300v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the method of Van Woerden \cite{woerden} to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\GLo-$equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\GLo$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\rint)$ obtained by Soul\'e \cite{soule_hermitian_bounds} and Houriet \cite{Juliet_PHD}. We emphasise the improvement of the general bound for $F=\mathbb Q$, unchanged since Soul\'e's work, and the independence of the discriminant exponent from the field degree for totally real and CM fields.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro de la Torre Dur\'an

item.title: A general L\^e--Siersma formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.06340v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the comparison between a Milnor fibre of a function $f$ and its section by the zero locus of a second function $s$ in a general ambient variety $\mathcal{X}$. We give a formula that generalizes those of L\^e and Siersma, expressing the difference of their Euler characteristics as a sum of local contributions associated with the critical points of the restriction of $s$. We provide an algebraic formula in the case that $\mathcal{X}$ is {smooth of pure dimension outside $f^{-1}(0)$}, and show some applications and examples.
item.dc:creator: R. Gim\'enez Conejero, J. J. Nu\~no-Ballesteros

item.title: Floer theory on based loops and fundamental groups of Lagrangians in $\mathbb{C}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2611.06574v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We obtain new constraints on the topology of Lagrangian submanifolds in the standard symplectic vector space $\mathbb{C}^n$ using Floer theory on the based loop space, generalizing a theorem of Fukaya-Irie. In particular, we show that non-trivial connected sums of closed, spin, aspherical manifolds of even dimensions do not admit Lagrangian embeddings into $\mathbb{C}^n$. A feature of the proof is that the obstructedness of the Floer theory is used to constrain the fundamental group of the Lagrangian.
item.dc:creator: Shuhao Li

item.title: Chewing gums, snakes and candle cakes
item.description: arXiv:2605.12572v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The aim of these lecture notes, based on lectures given by the second author at the CIME school in Cetraro, is to illustrate a range of ideas surrounding higher Teichmuller spaces of Riemann surfaces with marked boundaries through explicit and computationally tractable examples. After reviewing the classical Teichmuller space of hyperbolic Riemann surfaces with boundary and its combinatorial description in terms of Thurston shear coordinates on a fat-graph, we explain how the bordered cusped Teichmuller space arises as a confluent limit when two boundary components in the Riemann surface collide via the so-called chewing-gum move giving rise to a candle cake. We then revisit these constructions from the Fock-Goncharov perspective, explaining snake calculus for transport matrices in PSL_n(R) and explain how the chewing gum move is the inverse of amalgamation. Rather than focusing on formal proofs, our goal is to illustrate the underlying theorems and constructions in a concrete and intuitive way.
item.dc:creator: Benedetta Facciotti, Marta Mazzocco, Nikita Nikolaev

item.title: 2-Linearizability of Geometric 3-Manifold Groups Over Commutative Rings
item.description: arXiv:2608.01532v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The fundamental groups of compact 3-manifolds are known to be residually finite. Feng Luo conjectured that a stronger statement is true, by only allowing finite groups of the form $\mathrm{PGL}(2,R)$, where $R$ is a finite commutative ring. In earlier work, this conjecture was disproven in full generality. The conjecture arose in the context of orientable connected compact 3-manifolds which are geometrizable. By constructing explicit faithful linear representations using rings with nilpotent elements, we demonstrate that the conjecture holds for six of the eight Thurston model geometries, namely all but $\mathbb{S}^3$ and $\widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2}$. In the case of $\mathbb{S}^3$, the conjecture holds if we replace $\mathrm{PGL}(2,R)$ with $\mathrm{GL}(2,R)$. A spherical counterexample for the projective variant is the Poincar\'{e} homology sphere $\Sigma(2,3,5)$. In the case of $\widetilde{\mathrm{SL}_2}$, the conjecture fails to hold for both the projective and non-projective variants; a counterexample is provided by the Brieskorn sphere $\Sigma(2,3,7)$.
item.dc:creator: Montek Singh Gill

item.title: Hexagon decompositions and the Weil-Petersson metric
item.description: arXiv:2609.31278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an explicit quasi-isometry from the flip graph of triangulations $\mathscr{F}_{g,n}$ to the $\epsilon$-thick part of Teichm\"uller space equipped with the Teichm\"uller metric, by mapping each ideal triangulation to the hyperbolic surface whose shearing coordinates along that triangulation are all equal to zero. Extending this construction, we obtain a quasi-isometry $Q$ from the hexagon graph $\mathscr{H}_{g,n}$ to the augmented Teichm\"uller space $\overline{\operatorname{Teich}}_{g,n}$ equipped with the Weil-Petersson metric, and we estimate its width, that is, the Hausdorff distance between $Q(\mathscr{H}_{g,n})$ and $\overline{\operatorname{Teich}}_{g,n}$. By bounding the Weil-Petersson distance along grafting rays, and by using an analogue for ideal triangulations of Wolpert's upper bound on the Weil-Petersson distance to a stratum, we show that the width is at most of order $\sqrt{(g+n)\log(g+n)}$. We also provide an explicit projection from any point in $\overline{\operatorname{Teich}}_{g,n}$ to the thick part of boundary strata, maintaining simultaneous control over the Weil-Petersson distance and the shearing coordinates.
item.dc:creator: Marie Abadie

item.title: Singular Loci of SL2(C)-Representation Varieties of Torus Knot Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.32064v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $T(q,p)=\langle x,y\mid x^p=y^q\rangle$, where $p,q>1$ are relatively prime, and let \[ R=\Hom(T(q,p),\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb C)). \] We compute the integral homology of the singular locus of $R$. We show that this locus has complex dimension $2$ and is a disjoint union of $\mu=(p-1)(q-1)$ smooth affine surfaces, each homotopy equivalent to the two-dimensional sphere. Consequently, \[ H_0(\Sing R;\Z)\cong H_2(\Sing R;\Z)\cong\Z^\mu, \] and all remaining homology groups vanish. Thus both nonzero Betti numbers equal the first Betti number of the Milnor fiber of the plane curve singularity $z^p+w^q=0$, namely its Milnor number $\mu$.
item.dc:creator: S. Liriano

item.title: Linking-form splitting and four-dimensional genera of knots
item.description: arXiv:2610.40183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By Gilmer's splitting lemma, the linking form of a rational homology sphere that bounds a 4-manifold is the orthogonal sum of a metabolic summand and a summand presented by a form of the rank of the intersection form. The lemma underlies Gilmer's slice genus theorem and the rank criteria of Murakami-Yasuhara and Gilmer-Livingston for nonorientable surfaces and the 4-dimensional clasp number. We show that the lemma and these results, as stated, are false. For each prime $p \equiv 3 \pmod 8$ we construct knots bounding smooth M\"obius bands, and knots bounding smooth punctured tori with clasp number one, whose linking forms have no such summand of rank at most two. We then determine what remains true: the lemma holds up to Witt equivalence and for cube-free orders, and its conclusions about summands hold away from exceptional primes and for orientable surfaces of genus at least two. Finally, we find the optimal Witt-class bound for the topological nonorientable 4-genus.
item.dc:creator: Seong-Jin Lee

item.title: Embedded topological triviality of separable families of singularities
item.description: arXiv:2511.23185v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Understanding how singularities behave under small perturbations is a central theme in singularity theory. In this paper, we study separable families $f_s=f_0+\rho(s)\varphi$ of analytic function-germs on a germ of a complex analytic space $(X,0)$, and we give sufficient conditions for them to admit a topological trivialization. Our results extend previous work by the third author and collaborators, moving from abstract triviality to the embedded setting. As an application, we obtain new instances of topological stability, including a class of $\mu$-constant deformations. These findings provide a new perspective on the long-standing $\mu$-constant conjecture, one of the major open problems in the field.
item.dc:creator: R. Gim\'enez Conejero, Andreas Lind, Aur\'elio Menegon

item.title: On Realisability of Twisted Homology
item.description: arXiv:2607.24462v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the question of when a homology or cohomology class with twisted integer coefficients of a manifold $X$ is realised by a submanifold. While this question is classical in nature, providing an answer requires relatively modern techniques from parametrised homotopy theory. More specifically, we introduce cobordism classes twisted by a coefficient system and then define a twisted Thom space $\operatorname{M^\mathrm{tw}O}(n)$ over $\operatorname{BO}(1)$, which serves as the classifying object for this cobordism theory under a twisted Pontryagin-Thom construction. As a result, a twisted homology class is realisable if and only if its Poincar\'e dual is the image of the twisted Thom class in $\operatorname{M^\mathrm{tw}O}(n)$ under a parametrised map $X \to \operatorname{M^\mathrm{tw}O}(n)$ over $\operatorname{BO}(1)$. By showing that $\operatorname{M^\mathrm{tw}O}(n)$ is parametrised homotopy equivalent to the unbased homotopy orbits of $\operatorname{MSO}(n)$ under the orientation-reversing involution, we are able to construct its parametrised Postnikov tower to derive obstructions to realisability. We conclude by giving the first known examples of non-realisable integer homology classes in non-orientable manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Mark Grant, Michael Jung, Baylee Schutte

item.title: Closed geodesics in homology classes modulo sublattices
item.description: arXiv:2608.26311v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ be a Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surface of genus $g$, and let $\Gamma \subset \mathbb{Z}^{2g}$ be a lattice of prime index $q$. We study the distribution of primitive closed geodesics in homology classes mod $\Gamma$ in the large genus limit. Averaging over all lattices of index $q$, with $q \to \infty$, we compute all the centered moments of the corresponding weighted counting functions, and exhibit a transition between Poisson and Gaussian regimes (depending on whether $\frac{X}{q\log X}$, the expected number of primitive geodesics in a given homology class mod $\Gamma$, tends to $\lambda>0$ or $\infty$). We also study the unnormalized variance $G_M(X,\Gamma)$ of the counts among homology classes, and show that as $X \to \infty$, averaged over all lattices of prime index $q$, it is asymptotic to $X\log X$ in the large genus limit. These results are analogous to phenomena arising in the distribution of primes in arithmetic progressions.
item.dc:creator: Noam Pirani

item.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We give a short proof that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\lfloor4(n-1)/3\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings. We also give bipartite plane graphs showing that the coefficient $4/3$ is best possible under the local hypotheses used in the proof.
item.dc:creator: D\'aniel G\'abor Simon
